Subject: QuickShop call recap — throughput shape + initial recommendation

Team — quick post-call notes from today’s discovery with Alex & Priya at QuickShop (15:00 PT):

Summary of the ask
- Use case: product search and cart-ranking at checkout for QuickShop web & mobile. Low-latency user interactions during peak sale windows (Black Friday–style spikes).
- Target SLO: 95th percentile <= 120 ms for the inference step (end-to-end app goals are tighter but they want inference under 120 ms).
- Peak profile: bursts to ~250 QPS for ~10–20 minute windows, baseline ~15–25 QPS.
- Payload: prompts average 220 tokens, ratio of short/long sequences ~70/30.

Constraints and risks noted
- Timeline: pilot wanted in 3 weeks; production in 8–10 weeks if pilot goes well.
- Security: QuickShop is SOC 2 Type II in progress; they asked about Private VPC timeline but prefer not to delay pilot.
- Procurement: finance wants a simple pilot commitment; they asked for a cost estimate for both hosted and dedicated paths.

My read / recommended next step
- Start with a focused hosted API pilot but with a dedicated-reserved buffer for peak windows (burst capacity) and strict routing policies. This gets them running quickly and lets us measure real QPS shape. If the pilot shows consistent sustained QPS above our hosted cost break-even, we propose a Dedicated reserved pool for production.

Action items
1) Ben — can you draft a 2-week pilot benchmark plan (latency/throughput matrix, KV/prefix caching settings to test, and what we'll collect) and stub in estimated costs for hosted vs dedicated? Attach that as a one-pager. (Due: Tue 05/11)
2) Kim — confirm whether we can offer a burst reservation for two 20-minute windows per day without full Dedicated onboarding; list any config limits. (Due: Tue 05/11)
3) Alex/Priya — please send the QPS sample CSV and any historical logs (attached: QuickShop said they'd send CSV after call).

Attachments: call recording referenced, sample QPS CSV will be attached to their reply.

Thanks — Tessa

--
Tessa Morgan

Tessa — thanks for the write-up. Draft notes from my side below; attaching a concise pilot-benchmark-plan PDF (stub) for internal review.

Technical proposal (short)
- Pilot goal: validate 95p latency at target QPS bursts and confirm batching and prefix/KV cache effectiveness.
- Phases:
  1) Hosted pilot (2 weeks): use Redwood hosted API with the following config:
     - Model: rwd-open-13B (quantized profile)
     - Autoscaling: Min 2 replicas, max burst to an isolated pool that can sustain 300 QPS for 15 minutes
     - Caching: enable prefix caching for repeated prompts (we'll try TTL 5–15s), KV cache warmup via synthetic traffic
  2) If pilot shows >60% of total token cost reduction with caching and peak tail risk still high, move to Dedicated reserved capacity for production.

Metrics we'll collect
- Per-route p95/p99 inference latency (token vs end-to-end request), throughput per second, GPU utilization, batching factors per replica, KV hit rate, cost per 1M tokens.
- We'll run three synthetic bursts based on their CSV (attached) and one 24-hour steady-state run to calibrate autoscaling thresholds.

Cost notes (very rough)
- Hosted pilot (2 weeks): minor usage cost + temporary burst reservation fee (one-time configuration) — estimated to be <= 5k for pilot.
- Dedicated (production commit): upfront reserved capacity + baseline monthly charge — detailed numbers require exact qps and concurrency posture.

Questions for QuickShop
- Can they provide a 48-72 hour sampled logs export (traffic by minute) in addition to the CSV? That will let us size reserved pool.
- Are any requests synchronous with third-party services (latency compounding) or purely internal inference latency?

Attachment: pilot-benchmark-plan.pdf (stub) — contains matrix of runs and measurement points.

-ben

--

Tessa / Ben — thanks for the clear notes. Attached is the CSV sample (qshop-qps-sample.csv) — per-minute QPS over the last 30 days; the spikes are obviously our concern. A few clarifications from our side:

- We can provide a 72-hour raw log export (anonymized) by EOD Wednesday.
- Our engineering constraint: we prefer not to re-architect client-side retries during the pilot. So any pilot approach should tolerate our current retry/backoff behavior.
- Security: SOC 2 report is in progress; we can do Hosted pilot while SOC 2 is finalizing. Private VPC/on-prem is a hard requirement for production (policy) but procurement overhead is large — we want to avoid gating the pilot on that.

Preference and asks
- We prefer a hosted-first pilot if Redwood can demonstrate controlled tail latency during their synthetic bursts. If it looks close, we'll move fast to Dedicated for production.
- Please include an explicit fallback policy in the pilot plan (e.g., auto-fallback to smaller model or queueing) so our product team is comfortable in case of sustained overload during sales events.

Attaching: qshop-qps-sample.csv (per-minute QPS sample, 60 KB), historical spike snapshot image (spike-20270412.png).

Thanks — Alex

Alex / Priya — great, thanks for the CSV and the 72-hour log offer. Confirming our agreed pilot approach and next steps so everyone has a single source of truth:

Pilot plan (what Redwood will run)
- Kickoff: Thu 05/13 — two-week hosted-first performance pilot.
- Configuration: Redwood hosted API with temporary burst reservation to support up to 320 QPS sustained for 20-minute windows, autoscaling thresholds tuned to react within 60s for spike onset.
- Models/ops: rwd-open-13B quantized; Kv/prefix caching enabled; fallback policy configured to degrade to a smaller quantized model and return soft-queued responses if sustained overload > 5 minutes.
- Measurements: p50/p95/p99 inference latency, GPU batching factors, KV hit rate, cost per 1M tokens, and observed queueing events. We’ll run synthetic bursts mimicking your CSV (3 runs) and 24-hour steady capture.

What we need from QuickShop
1) 72-hour anonymized logs export (EOD Wed 05/12) — to size the reserved buffer.
2) Test account/API key for a scoped subset of traffic or a replay endpoint (sample creds ok for pilot).
3) Contact in procurement for a short pilot agreement (one-page MSA addendum) — Alex, you mentioned finance wants minimal friction.

Timeline and next sync
- We’ll send the pilot benchmark plan (with explicit fallback behavior and cost estimate) by Tue 05/11 (Ben noted he’ll deliver that).
- Kickoff call to align scope: Thu 05/13 10:00 PT — 30m. I’ll send a calendar invite once receipt of logs/test keys.

If the pilot shows sustained peaks that make hosted economics unfavorable, we’ll present a Dedicated reserved proposal with capacity numbers and a migration runbook (expect ~2–3 week lead for Dedicated provisioning). Private VPC will be scoped for production (policy requirement) but will not block the pilot.

Next steps (short list)
- Alex: share logs and a test/replay endpoint (today).
- Ben: finalize pilot-benchmark-plan PDF and cost ballpark (today/Tue).
- Kim: confirm burst reservation ability and any limits (today/Tue).
- Tessa: send calendar invite for Thu kickoff once test creds received.

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.

Best,
Tessa
